newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO ruling expected in US-EU banana row.
newsitem.headline: WTO ruling expected in US-EU banana row.

text.p: A World Trade Organisation panel is expected to deliver its initial ruling on Tuesday in a U.S.-European Union dispute over the EU's banana import regime, trade diplomats said.
The findings, officially to remain confidential until a final ruling but which often leak, will be delivered to the WTO missions of the two trade powers in Geneva for transmission to capitals.

There was no immediate indication of the outcome of the panel's nearly 10 months of deliberations on the issue. Caribbean nations argue it could deal a severe blow to their economies if the U.S. complaint is upheld.

Panels under the WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), twice found Brussels was violating open trading rules by gearing the market to favour bananas from former colonies of EU member states.
Those findings were handed down following complaints to GATT from Latin American banana producers.
Although not a producer, the United States moved into the dispute in 1995, arguing that the EU regime discriminates against U.S.-based banana marketing companies.
It has been joined in its action by Ecuador, the world's largest exporter, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico.
The EU extends preferential treatment to bananas from 12 countries of the African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) group under Brussels 1993 Lome Convention.
Under WTO procedures, after receiving the three-man panel's interim ruling, the EU and the United States forward comments on the outcome and the panel then issues its final finding.
This can be appealed by either side, extending the process for several more months.
